t: French Revolution: After being found guilty of high treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined in Paris.
The Russian Empire and the Kingdom of Prussia partitioned the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth for the second time.
Andreas Joseph Hofmann proclaimed the Republic of Mainz, becoming the first republican state in Germany.
Scottish explorer Alexander Mackenzie reached the Pacific coast at Bella Coola, British Columbia, completing the first recorded transcontinental crossing of North America north of Mexico.
The Louvre in Paris, today the world's most-visited museum, opened with an exhibition of 537 paintings and 184 objets d'art.
War of the Pyrenees: Forces from the French Army of the Eastern Pyrenees defeated two divisions of the Army of Catalonia, ending the furthest Spanish encroachment in their invasion of Roussillon.
French Revolution: After a month-long siege, the leaders of Lyon surrendered, ending their revolt against the National Convention.
War of the First Coalition: The two-day Battle of Wattignies concluded with Jean-Baptiste Jourdan leading French forces to victory over Prince Josias of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.
French Revolution: Playwright, journalist and outspoken feminist Olympe de Gouges was guillotined.
